A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 23-page versions of the same BORSCH study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–O are readable and matchable, including the image-based appendix examples.

before.justification: v2 reports original QA/VQA experiments, pretraining-corpus analyses, and dish-description evaluations with human validation in Sections 4–5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental and data-analysis results, including the supplementary evaluations and human-validation results.

M1.justification: The bootstrapped dataset-construction procedure and description-evaluation pipeline using FLUX.1-dev and DiNOv2 remain unchanged. Appendix H's input-wording correction does not introduce a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Russian/Ukrainian BORSCH data, 433-dish parallel subset, English comparison data, and evaluation tasks. WORLD-CUISINES is explicitly named in v3 but corresponds to the already cited Winata et al. dataset.

E2.justification: The same Llama-3.1-70B and Qwen2-72B text models and Llama-3.2-90B and Qwen2-VL-72B vision models participate in the comparisons. The added CUS-QA citation is not an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix H corrects the reported input from the dish's 'name and origin' to 'name and images.' This is a limited protocol-description correction: v2 Section 4.1, Figure 13, and Tables 5–6 already specify images plus names, so it does not establish changed execution or rerunning.

E4.justification: The code-mixing and co-occurrence analyses, contamination assessment, dish-name input comparison, human validation, alternative-metric analyses, and qualitative examples are retained unchanged, including Appendices C, H, and J.

E5.justification: Annotation-agreement statistics, correlation reporting, and statistical displays are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises run/seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or significance testing relative to the other.

E6.justification: The numerical results, plotted trends, and qualitative findings match throughout. For example, Table 3 retains Pearson correlations of 0.82/0.82 for Llama and 0.78/0.81 for Qwen in Russian/Ukrainian, and Figure 19 retains identical examples and similarity scores.

T1.justification: The co-occurrence definitions and mathematical formulations are unchanged, including the Jaccard, Dice, and overlap formulas in Appendix J.4, Equations (1)–(3). No assumptions, proofs, or theoretical results are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same dataset contribution and claims about language-associated origin predictions, pretraining co-occurrences, code mixing, and the limited correlation between QA and description-generation performance.

C2.justification: The explanations involving code mixing and web-scraping errors remain unchanged. Both versions retain the same limitations concerning narrow linguistic scope, geographic skew, and evaluation of dish origins/names rather than subjective attributes.

D1.justification: The prompts, annotation instructions, SPARQL query, model configurations, decoding parameters, hardware/runtime details, and code/data access statements are unchanged. Appendix H's correction adds no implementation information unavailable elsewhere in v2.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Libovický et al. (2025), CUS-QA, with a corresponding reference. It also explicitly names WORLD-CUISINES where v2 already cited Winata et al. (2024); the 20.8% coverage comparison and broader novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits are localized: explicit WORLD-CUISINES naming, the Appendix H correction, a comma in Appendix E, and a memorial sentence in the acknowledgments. Section organization and the scientific narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Small line and column reflow changes appear in related work and the references following the text additions. Figures 1–19 and Tables 1–8 retain their designs, captions, content, and placement; there is no substantive graphical revision.

improvement.justification: Correcting Appendix H makes its input description consistent with Section 4.1, Figure 13, and the prompt tables, removing a misleading reference to supplying the dish's origin. Explicitly naming WORLD-CUISINES also improves identification of an existing comparison. These are limited clarity gains; the scientific methods, evidence, and conclusions remain unchanged.
